{"status": "success", "summary": "Split the task into its two independent parts and delegated each to its own worker, then integrated the results and wrote the dependent notes file myself.

Team: sum_worker (task t-306235b0-2e52-411b-b649-094688c96516) and words_worker (task t-662507db-74a6-4aaf-b302-015cda93fef0), both on the shared workspace. Both settled SUCCEEDED; I re-verified their outputs independently before integrating.

Files written:
- out/sum.txt = "44\n" (sum of 17, -4, 23, 8 in data/a.txt)
- out/words.txt = "Apple\napple\nfig\npear\nplum\n" (5 unique words, case-sensitive lexicographic order: uppercase 'A' sorts before lowercase 'a')
- out/notes.txt (my integration step, depends on both results) = one line: "Sum of integers in data/a.txt = 44; unique case-sensitively sorted words from data/b.txt = 5 (Apple, apple, fig, pear, plum)."

Commands I really ran (integration/verification):
- `cat out/sum.txt; cat out/words.txt; wc -l out/words.txt` -> 44 / 5 words
- `awk '{s+=$1} END{print s}' data/a.txt` -> 44
- `python3 -c ...` recomputing both: sum 44 == file_sum 44; words 5 == file_words ['Apple','apple','fig','pear','plum']
- `ls -la out/`, `cat out/notes.txt`, `wc -l out/notes.txt` -> notes.txt is exactly 1 line

Worker-reported verification (accepted, cross-checked against my own recomputation): words_worker ran `tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' < data/b.txt | sed '/^$/d' | LC_ALL=C sort -u` and `diff` (exit 0) plus a Python check; sum_worker ran `awk` and a Python check, both giving 44.", "evidence": ["out/sum.txt contains 44", "out/words.txt contains Apple/apple/fig/pear/plum", "out/notes.txt single-line note", "awk '{s+=$1} END{print s}' data/a.txt -> 44", "python3 recompute: sum 44 file_sum 44; words 5 file_words ['Apple','apple','fig','pear','plum']", "task t-306235b0-2e52-411b-b649-094688c96516 SUCCEEDED", "task t-662507db-74a6-4aaf-b302-015cda93fef0 SUCCEEDED"]}
